interpretation: If what is deprived of an ability is unable, what is not coming to be will be unable to come to be; and whoever says that what is unable to come to be is or will be speaks falsely, 'for this is what unable meant'. Read as: what is being moved toward r is able to be r. Aristotle presents it as following from the meaning of 'unable' (ἀδύνατον); the reading applies it to the outcome r of a present motion.
